41b020c80f528194b2bdf727773b9dce:
DISSIPATE No. 8 OF NINE NEVADA DEPRESSIONS — Michael Heizer, 1968.

Five shallow trenches lined with wood, cut into the dry lakebed of Black Rock Desert in Nevada and placed as if matches had been dropped on the ground. Part of a series of nine works across the Nevada desert, made to be eroded and lost. Land art at its beginning: sculpture made by taking material away.

#michaelheizer #landart #nevada #desert #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528110ab4de4be027d17e7:
LE CHÂTEAU DES PYRÉNÉES — René Magritte, 1959.

A huge boulder hangs above a stormy sea, with a small castle growing out of its top. Magritte paints the impossible with the calm precision of a postcard, so that gravity seems to be the thing that is wrong. The painting is in the Israel Museum, Jerusalem.

#renemagritte #surrealism #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528159bd29d44330043cc3:
IL MONUMENTO CONTINUO — Superstudio, 1969.

A single gridded structure that wraps the whole planet, crossing deserts, cities and seas without changing. The Florentine group drew it in collages as a critique of architecture's will to order everything. One of the founding images of Radical Architecture.

#superstudio #radicalarchitecture #collage #utopia #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281abb253febb7d4c767e:
STRIKE: TO ROBERTA AND RUDY — Richard Serra, 1969–71.

A single plate of hot-rolled steel, eight by twenty-four feet, wedged into the corner of a room and held there only by the two walls. It cuts the space in two, and as you walk around it the plate turns from surface to edge and back. Now at the Guggenheim, New York.

#richardserra #sculpture #steel #minimalism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52810f888fcaa6e003f4d6:
RODEN CRATER — James Turrell, since 1979.

An extinct volcanic cone in the Painted Desert of Arizona, bought by Turrell in 1979 and reshaped from inside into an observatory for the naked eye. Tunnels and chambers frame the sky, the sun and the moon. Still in progress after more than four decades.

#jamesturrell #rodencrater #landart #light #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528197842cc4c143d6ddd4:
THE ELEMENTAL HOUSE — Charles Jencks with Buzz Yudell and Charles Moore, 1982. Rustic Canyon, Los Angeles.

A 1950s ranch house reworked around the four elements, earth, water, air and fire. Its pool is shaped like the State of California. Postmodern symbolism, played with a straight face.

#charlesjencks #buzzyudell #postmodernism #losangeles #pool #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52818a82ffca621a4a5dff:
MODULAR CUBE — Sol LeWitt, 1965.

An open lattice of identical square cells, the same in every direction. LeWitt chose the cube because it is the least expressive form there is, and so it lets the system be the subject. The idea is the machine that makes the art.

#sollewitt #minimalism #conceptualart #sculpture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281b8b4befdbfa6a38214:
ARCHITECTURE OBLIQUE — Claude Parent, 1960s–70s.

With Paul Virilio, Parent proposed living on inclined planes instead of flat floors: walking would become climbing, and the body would feel every move. Built examples are few, the church of Sainte-Bernadette in Nevers (1966) among them, but the drawings remain.

#claudeparent #paulvirilio #functionoblique #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281c0a2ccc646943ab3ed:
BURGERWEESHUIS (AMSTERDAM ORPHANAGE) — Aldo van Eyck, 1955–1960.

A small city for children: repeated domed units grouped in clusters, with interior streets and courtyards between them. Van Eyck called it a house like a small city and a city like a large house. A founding work of Dutch Structuralism.

#aldovaneyck #structuralism #amsterdam #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281abb7eee7eecf4a6da9:
WEISS AUF SCHWARZ (WHITE ON BLACK) — Wassily Kandinsky, 1930.

Painted in his last years at the Bauhaus in Dessau: thin, floating geometric shapes on a black ground. For Kandinsky black was a silence without future, against which every color sounds sharper.

#wassilykandinsky #bauhaus #abstraction #painting #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528197a3cdc5169ebb2d78:
NO-STOP CITY — Archizoom Associati, 1969–1972.

An endless, homogeneous interior, lit and air-conditioned like a supermarket, where furniture and tents replace buildings. Archizoom drew it with a typewriter, as a grid of characters, to show the city as pure quantity. A radical critique of the modern metropolis.

#archizoom #nostopcity #radicalarchitecture #andreabranzi #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281058789c1db3c70594b:
THE INCOMPLETE TRUTH — Damien Hirst, 2006.

A white dove with spread wings, suspended in formaldehyde inside a glass and steel case. The sign of the Holy Spirit and of peace becomes a specimen.

#damienhirst #formaldehyde #contemporaryart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a89843d0fb13ce12c9:
CONCETTO SPAZIALE, ATTESE — Lucio Fontana, 1963.

A monochrome canvas opened by clean cuts with a blade. Fontana's slashes are not destruction but an opening onto the space behind the painting. 'Attese' means waitings.

#luciofontana #spazialismo #concettospaziale #italianart #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281829890dbabe9980e18:
TEATRO DEL MONDO — Aldo Rossi, 1979–80.

A floating wooden theatre built for the Venice Biennale, towed across the lagoon on a barge and moored in front of the Punta della Dogana. It belonged to the city for one season, then it was dismantled. Rossi's most poetic building, made to disappear.

#aldorossi #teatrodelmondo #venezia #biennale #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528177b6cfe26e348c0d0d:
STILL LIFE — Tom Wesselmann, 1962.

From the series of Still Lifes begun in 1962: collage and paint on board, with supermarket products and advertising images arranged like a Dutch still life. American abundance seen in the flat language of the billboard.

#tomwesselmann #popart #stilllife #collage #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52816b8ad0c36b54152947:
BARCELONA PAVILION — Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, 1929.

German pavilion for the International Exposition in Barcelona: free-standing walls of onyx and green marble, chromed cruciform columns, and a reflecting pool. Demolished in 1930 and rebuilt on the same site in 1986.

#miesvanderrohe #barcelonapavilion #modernism #architecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281a78b58eb442374f9b9:
STILL LIFE WITH GOLDFISH — Roy Lichtenstein, 1972.

Lichtenstein quotes Matisse's goldfish bowl and translates it into Ben-Day dots, black outlines and flat color. Painting about painting, in the language of comic strips.

#roylichtenstein #popart #matisse #stilllife #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528151b99cc959790f273e:
THE BIG DUCK — Flanders, Long Island, New York, 1931.

A building in the shape of a duck, built by a duck farmer to sell ducks and eggs. Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown and Steven Izenour used it in Learning from Las Vegas (1972) as their 'duck': a building whose form is its sign, against the 'decorated shed'.

#bigduck #venturiscottbrown #learningfromlasvegas #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281d097bae2bf94d827c9:
BAUHAUS — Herbert Bayer, 1925.

Bayer studied at the Bauhaus in Weimar and in 1925 became head of the new printing and advertising workshop in Dessau. He designed the 'universal' alphabet in lower case only. Typography reduced to geometry.

#herbertbayer #bauhaus #typography #graphicdesign #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528195921efeead1ecc049:
SCANDIANO — Luigi Ghirri, 1971.

Ghirri was born in Scandiano, near Reggio Emilia, and began photographing in the early 1970s, while still working as a surveyor. His Emilia is made of signs, walls and empty corners, looked at with quiet attention.

#luigighirri #fotografia #emilia #italianphotography #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528116a057fbc81ff022db:
HOUSE AT MINAMI-AOYAMA — Kunihiko Hayakawa, Tokyo.

Hayakawa built his architecture around the 'landscapes that architecture produces' in the city. His Tokyo houses read like fragments of stage set, layered planes and colors in a dense, fragmented city.

#kunihikohayakawa #tokyo #japanesearchitecture #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f52813781cbf2465577559b:
I AM A MONUMENT — Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown, 1972.

A drawing from Learning from Las Vegas: a plain shed with a huge sign that announces 'I am a monument'. The decorated shed, where the meaning is written on the building rather than built into it.

#venturiscottbrown #learningfromlasvegas #decoratedshed #postmodernism #mnemotheca
41b020c80f5281f1885fd46b51436404:
CARCERI D'INVENZIONE, PLATE VII — Giovanni Battista Piranesi, c. 1745–1761.

The Drawbridge: stairs, bridges and walkways climb through a vast, impossible prison. The Carceri were first etched around 1745–50 and reworked, darker and deeper, in 1761.

#piranesi #carceri #etching #imaginaryarchitecture #mnemotheca
41b020c80f528127b663eb3ea3abe386:
PARTHENOPE — Paolo Sorrentino, 2024.

Born in the sea off Naples in 1950, Parthenope crosses decades of the city's beauty and decay. Sorrentino films Naples the way he films his heroine: sunlit, theatrical, always slightly out of reach. Cinematography by Daria D'Antonio.

#mnemotheca
